title: What Is Code?
summary: Learn what programs are and how they execute top-to-bottom.

steps.title: What Are Programs?
steps.markdownContent: Programs are instructions a computer follows. Just like a recipe tells a chef how to bake a cake, a program tells a computer what to do.

quickCheck.question: What tells a computer or robot what actions to perform?
options: A set of instructions called code or a program
quickCheck.explanation: Computers follow written instructions called code or programs to know what actions to take!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Just like a recipe tells a baker how to make cookies, computer instructions tell machines what to do.

quickCheck.question: In what order do computer programs usually follow instructions?
options: One step at a time from top to bottom
quickCheck.explanation: Programs execute sequentially, running one instruction after another from top to bottom!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: When you read a book or follow a recipe, you read line by line from top to bottom.

steps.title: Statements
steps.markdownContent: A single instruction in code is called a statement. In Arduino (C++), every statement must end in a semicolon `;`.

steps.title: Top-to-Bottom Flow
steps.markdownContent: Programs run top-to-bottom, one statement at a time. The computer does exactly what you tell it—nothing more.

steps.title: Deconstruct a Program
steps.markdownContent: Let's look at a simple program and break it down into statements.

steps.title: Knowledge Check
steps.markdownContent: Test what you learned about programs and statements.

questions.question: What is a program?
questions.explanation: A program is a set of instructions a computer follows to perform a task.

questions.question: What must every statement end with in C++?
questions.explanation: Every statement must end with a semicolon.

questions.question: How do programs run?
questions.explanation: Programs execute sequentially from top to bottom.
